knowledge: Reading workload pod listings: the READY column (a/b containers ready) and the RESTARTS column (count, with the most recent restart time) are what single out the unhealthy instance — typically one pod at 'READY 1/2' with a rising restart count; the phase word (Running) alone does not distinguish it.

Reading the error-log output: it arrives as deduplicated patterns (count / ratio per group) whose sample lines hold the raw text — read the sample text verbatim as the mechanism lead (a panic / exception line states the failure itself); the counts only tell how dominant each pattern is.

Reading the alert output: it is self-describing — each alert names the entity, an anomaly class (e.g. RESOURCE_SATURATION / LATENCY_DEGRADATION / THROUGHPUT_DROP) and an evidence line comparing baseline vs current (e.g. 'Normal=4.74ms -> Current=37.82ms (+697.2%)'); the comparison inside the text is the reading — the alert identifies where and what kind of anomaly.

Telemetry-led reading: pair the alerted entity with the object-layer listings — if that entity reads normal (all running, no restarts, endpoints bound), the break is not an unhealthy object; the signal lives at the metric level, and the object listing is the exclusion side of the pair.
basis: object listings vs alerts cross-reading (both visible)

knowledge: Reading a restarted container: its pod detail carries the last termination state — a reason and an exit code (e.g. OOMKilled 137 vs SIGTERM-by-kubelet 143) — read that field to classify why the container restarted before moving further down the chain.

Reading the code slot (Boutique only): service-first — list the recorded source files of the service named by the log sample, then fetch the specific file; the failing call / parameter is read off that source. The slot is closed by the source itself, not by a wider search.

Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Partial Service Unreachability.' enters the reachability chain: caller-side error logs → the caller's addressed endpoints → the target service's endpoint binding / pods → owner chain (deployment) → stage evidence. Walk the surfaces in that order; the first surface whose observation contradicts expectation is the break.
basis: query templates ↔ chain entry (dataset wording, model-side mapping)

knowledge: Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Service Availability Disruption.' uses the SAME reachability chain (it is overloaded across scheduling / startup / admission stages): walk caller logs → endpoints → pods; when the pods surface shows the pod never became ready, read its phase and events (FailedScheduling / FailedCreate / FailedMount / image-pull / probe) and follow that mechanism to the matching object surface. Discriminate on the chain, not on the wording.
basis: query templates ↔ chain entry (overloaded wording; discrimination happens on the chain)

knowledge: Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Service Performance Degradation.' enters the telemetry chain: read alerts first (entity + anomaly class + baseline/current comparison), then EXCLUDE the object layer for that entity (listings normal → the break is at the metric level). Gated by the scorer: alerts are a symptom pointer, not evidence — close the case on object-layer exclusion plus metric readings.
basis: query templates ↔ chain entry; scorer gate on GetAlerts credit (visible side)

knowledge: Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Service abnormal restart.' enters the health chain: restarts (pods surface: RESTARTS column) → last termination state (exit code class: 137 OOMKilled vs 143 SIGTERM) → probe / OOM evidence (pod events: 'Unhealthy' / 'Killing' messages; deployment probes config). The restarting pod's own record and the workload probe config are the two halves that close this chain.
basis: query templates ↔ chain entry (dataset wording, model-side mapping)

knowledge: Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Service latency increased significantly' enters the telemetry chain (as Performance Degradation): alerts → object-layer exclusion → metric readings. No object-layer break is expected; the closure is the metric comparison itself.

Symptom wording → entry chain — 'Service quality degradation.' enters the telemetry chain (as Performance Degradation): alerts every time; pair the alerted entity with object-layer listings to exclude object faults before concluding on the metric reading.
